Let confirmed code fields wrap with enlarged clinical text

import pathlib,shutil,json
scratch=pathlib.Path("/home/saithat/Projects/run-tmp/merge-six-20261106")
source=scratch/"profile-after/cache";dest=pathlib.Path("/home/saithat/Projects/run-tmp/vgi-screen-check-cache")
counts={}
for kind in ["results","physical"]:
 n=0
 for file in (source/kind).rglob("*.json"):
  target=dest/file.relative_to(source)

 counts[kind]=n
print(json.dumps(counts));(scratch/"cache-seed.json").write_text(json.dumps(counts,indent=2)+"\n")
PY

limitations: Single measurements; not a statistical performance estimate.
Standalone revision has 819 distinct trees. Cross-revision batching deduplicates across all 33 revisions, so this wall time is not comparable to a per-revision average from the complete batch.

Additional native validation workers ran during the first two optimized batches, then were suspended for the rest of that profile. The final conformance run was restarted uninterrupted after suspension expired its per-call deadlines.
Historical approximately 90 seconds/revision serial baseline has no recorded cache temperature or fully pinned coverage, so an apples-to-apples historical regression ratio cannot be established.
An import-isolation startup experiment left startup near 0.75 seconds and was fully reverted.

preliminaryAttempts.name: generated-world HTTP routing
preliminaryAttempts.result: Stopped the initial broad desktop run after four banner timeouts exposed the server treating /runs/world/<id>/ as a completed recording. Added manifest-inventoried world reads and an HTTP regression retaining recorded-run fences and rejecting traversal/unlisted files. Full app unit suite and affected banner tests rerun, followed by a fresh complete desktop run. Certified clinical app hash remains unchanged by this server-only fix.

preliminaryAttempts.name: early Lake overlap
preliminaryAttempts.result: An early bounded check and trace test overlapped. Added a per-checkout lock for every Lake-invoking verification command and reran required checks sequentially.

preliminaryAttempts.name: native import isolation
preliminaryAttempts.result: No startup improvement (~0.75 seconds); entirely reverted. Diagnostic rebuild interrupted original unpinned readers with ENOENT. Those attempts discarded and rerun against an immutable matching binary.

preliminaryAttempts.name: canonical profiling suspension
preliminaryAttempts.result: Suspending its process expired 30-second native-call deadlines. Discarded the entire attempt and restarted the full six-worker suite uninterrupted; no result stitching or weakened assertions.

preliminaryAttempts.name: native-startup-fix receipt
preliminaryAttempts.result: Initial diagnostic command masked a build failure in its final shell status. Not counted as a pass; corrected build and complete restoration verified separately.

preliminaryAttempts.name: initial source integrations
preliminaryAttempts.result: Merged MAR fixture required the event return to expose state explicitly; completion goal codec lacked information-needs serializers; baseline audit paths referenced a lane checkout; validation fixture stopped at new effect floor; stored CURES probe bound prior binary; new native-batch parser required narrowing rather than a cast. Fixed causes and reran relevant checks.

preliminaryAttempts.name: comparison fixture and populated-select reflow
preliminaryAttempts.result: The second complete desktop run passed 180 tests, skipped 21 opt-in cases, and found two failures. The partial-index fixture missed prefix-pinned requests; fixed its route and asserted interception, retaining every fallback/day/frame expectation. A real populated frequency label clipped at 1280px/200% text. DOM inspection identified the confirmation wrapper; text-relative minimum tracks now include direct and confirmed code fields. All 47 default fidelity/physical/control checks pass. No assertion, field value or policy threshold was weakened. Renderer hash changed to the final binding, so cache population and warm recording installation/replay were repeated.
